grammarSchedule.why: `to be` is in lesson 1; stare is written as a gloss override, `sto[to be:stare]`, since the bank keys only essere
subject pronouns and essere are both in lesson 1, so a sentence can drop the pronoun from there on
molto, si and no are lesson 2, which is where the judgment and quantity adverbs start; qui and la follow in lesson 6 and sempre and mai in lesson 26
`the` (il) and `a/an` (un) are both in lesson 5, together with the first count nouns
lesson 5 pairs a masculine and a feminine noun with their articles: il libro, la casa
the topic includes avere, which lesson 5 teaches; the regular -are/-ere verbs follow in lessons 9 and 10
`here` and `there` arrive in lesson 6; esserci is written as a gloss on `to be`
questo and quello are the whole of lesson 6
chi, cosa, dove, quando, perché and come are the whole of lesson 7
`to be called` (chiamarsi) was moved into lesson 7, where `come` and `chi` make `Come si chiama la donna?` writable; alzarsi follows in lesson 20
scusi is in lesson 3; the noi-imperative needs a verb, and andare and fare arrive in lesson 8
lesson 7 gives the question words and lesson 8 the first verbs to invert with
per arrives in lesson 11 and the infinitives it governs are already taught in lessons 8 to 10
in, su, a, di, con, per are lesson 11; the articulated forms fuse them with the article from lesson 5
cardinals zero to nine are lesson 12; the ordinals primo, secondo, terzo come in lesson 46
lui and lei are in lesson 1, the atonic object forms in lesson 13
potere, volere and dovere are all in lesson 16
lesson 16 teaches `would like`; vorrei is written `[would like:volere]`
il caffè, invariable in the plural, is in lesson 17; la mano follows in 36 and il paio in 46
molti, tanto and poco are all in lesson 19
ho freddo and ho caldo need lesson 23; the age expression waits for `year` in lesson 28

lessons.theme: in the morning, in the evening
in front and in the middle
